authorised_by: bench owner, 2026-08-30 - the standing thermal instruction records possibly-thermal drift as a candidate rather than chasing it, so this arm needed the owner's decision and had been deferred across two sessions

firmware.note: Track B firmware identical - the only firmware-path commits between them are under apps/rtos_bringup (Track C, #45)

protocol: hot arm taken after ~2 h of continuous board work; board then idle 45 min (22:01-22:46) with no captures, no flashes, no console opens; reflashed to the same Track B image and remeasured immediately. Both arms are 12-24 min after a flash, so a reset is present in both.

within_image_test.reading: marginal on its own and should not be quoted as significant

pooled.caveat: pools across sessions and firmware images, and tonight established that images matter, so this is replication of a pattern rather than one clean experiment

conclusion: the drift is REST-REVERSIBLE. Incidence is high on a rested or fresh board and falls with continuous running, and it recovers after 45 minutes idle. That is the first positive result on this drift; the previous position was 'unexplained, one explanation offered and killed'.
not_claimed: that the mechanism is thermal - nothing here measures temperature
that 45 minutes is a characteristic time - one duration was tested
that the effect is this large; the clean within-image test is marginal
